What the person wants done with it is often clear from what they were doing a minute earlier.' Here the minute earlier is a deploy they were watching, so nothing needs asking — the one short question the skill reserves for an unclear paste is not owed. The act is therefore an observation, not an instruction: they reported a fact, they did not phrase an ask. The question is then whether the repair follows. 'Some observations carry their repair with them' sets the test as whether a competent colleague would need to ask what was wanted; a live TypeError in checkEntitlement moments after a deploy is the same shape as 'Production is returning 500s' — nobody pastes a fresh crash from their own deploy to be agreeable, and no colleague would ask whether the crash should be fixed. The repair follows beyond doubt, so the Director acts rather than merely filing evidence, and the exception in the observation row ('infer a repair job, unless the repair follows from the situation beyond doubt') is met. Nothing in the scenario names a repair already diagnosed and in flight, so the clause about a known failure reported again — 'the fix sent, the work still open, a fresh run under way' — does not apply and this does not land as a correction on running work; the deploy the person was watching is not itself an open task whose goal is being changed. That makes this newly accepted work: creates_work is true, attaches_to_existing_work is false, and one result is wanted — the crash stopped — which is one piece of work however many files it touches ('One instruction stays one piece of work even when it will touch six files'). Since a piece of work is accepted now, the operation line taken is the first that fits: admitting the ticket and taking it in hand in one call, ['T1','T2']. No idea half was voiced, so shelves_idea is false, and no new blocker is named — the crash is the work itself, not something only the person can clear. Specialists stay the smallest set the pipeline may need — the developer to fix the undefined read at billing.js:142, and the test author to choose the regression that proves it stays fixed.
